newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. names new consul general in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: U.S. names new consul general in Shanghai.

text.p: The U.S. government has named a new consul general in Shanghai, Raymond Burghardt, who will take up the post before the end of June, the consulate said in a statement on Wednesday.
Burghardt will replace Joseph Borich, who is due to leave in mid-June, consular officials said.
Burghardt most recently served as the U.S. deputy chief of mission in Manila from 1993 to 1996, the statement said.
He previously served as U.S. deputy chief of mission in Seoul, where he was also charge d'affaires for six months during his 1990 to 1993 posting, it said.

Burghardt was involved in consultations between the United States and South Korea on measures to deal with the threat posed by North Korea's programmes to develop nuclear weapons, and was a political counsellor in Beijing from 1987 to 1989, the statement said.

Borich, who has served as consul general in Shanghai since August 1994, will become executive director of the Washington State China Relations Council, which aims to improve business ties between the two countries, the officials said.
Borich is retiring from the foreign service to take up the private sector position, they said.
